items.stem: Which subsystem controls the direction a vehicle travels?
items.explanation: The guidance subsystem controls direction. A steering wheel, a rudder, and a navigation system are all part of guidance.

items.stem: A car rolls over a bump in the road, but the ride stays smooth and the body stays steady. Which subsystem is doing its job?
items.explanation: The suspension subsystem absorbs bumps and keeps the vehicle stable. Springs and shock absorbers let the wheels move while the body stays steady.

items.stem: Which subsystem provides the motion that moves a vehicle forward?
items.explanation: The propulsion subsystem provides motion. An engine, an electric motor, a propeller, and a jet engine are all forms of propulsion.

items.stem: The frame and body of a car hold all the other parts in place and give the vehicle its shape. These belong to which subsystem?
items.explanation: The structural subsystem supports the vehicle and holds its parts in place. The frame, body, and an airplane's wings are all structural.

items.stem: A driver presses the brake pedal and the car slows down. Braking is part of which subsystem?
items.explanation: The control subsystem regulates and monitors how the vehicle operates. Brakes, sensors, computers, and cruise control are all part of control.

items.stem: On an airplane, the wings help support the aircraft and give it shape. The wings are part of which subsystem?
items.explanation: The wings are part of the structural subsystem, which supports the vehicle. On a car this same subsystem is the frame and body.

items.stem: A car gets a flat tire. Why does this affect more than just the one wheel?

options.text: The subsystems interact, so trouble in one affects the others
Each subsystem works completely on its own
The tire is the only part that matters
Nothing else about the car changes at all

items.explanation: Because the subsystems depend on one another, a flat tire makes the car harder to steer and slower to stop. A failure in one subsystem reaches the whole vehicle.

items.stem: The rudder of a ship and the steering wheel of a car do a similar job. Which subsystem do they both belong to?
items.explanation: Both the rudder and the steering wheel control direction, so they belong to the guidance subsystem.

items.stem: Which statement best describes how a vehicle's subsystems work?

options.text: Each subsystem works alone with no connection to the others
No subsystem works alone; together they make one transportation system
Only the propulsion subsystem actually matters
A vehicle really has just one subsystem

items.explanation: No subsystem works alone. Each one has a different job, and through their interactions they work together as one transportation system.

items.stem: A jet engine, an electric motor, and a propeller are all examples of parts from which subsystem?
items.explanation: All three provide motion, so they are part of the propulsion subsystem. Different vehicles use different forms of propulsion to move.
